> a bit disappointing to see this closed

I thought this was a bug until I found this... how is this not implemented from the beginning...

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #45549: Cross-project session event bus + plugin-safe subscribe — overlaps directly on the missing parent lineage in session events and the integration observability gap (see point 3 there about carrying parentID on session events so consumers can build subagent trees)
- #44747: Subagent permission request silently dropped → parent stuck busy forever — related symptom where child-session permission events don't surface correctly to external consumers
- #13715: Permission asks from nested subagent sessions silently hang — related visibility gap for nested subagent events

Thanks for the pointers — I checked all three. None is an exact duplicate of this report, but there is real overlap with #45549 on one point.

- #44747: there the permission request is dropped and never reaches any client, leaving the parent turn hung (a runtime bug). In my case the events do reach external consumers — the problem is what they contain: child `session.error` / `permission.*` arrive with only the child session id, the root's own status stays `busy` for the whole subagent run, and nothing on the root session marks subagent start/recovery/completion. An integration can't tell a running (or auto-retrying) subagent from a parent actually waiting on the user.
- #13715: a TUI rendering bug (children() memo misses grandchild prompts, session hangs). No hang and no TUI involvement here — the subagent runs fine; the gap is in event payloads for external consumers.
- #45549: genuine overlap with its point 3. My capture confirms what #30043 describes: only `session.created` carries `info.parentID`; child `session.status` events carry no parent lineage at all, and the root session emits nothing between subagent start and completion. This report adds the concrete failure mode that gap causes downstream (herdr's pane plugin renders a child `session.error` during automatic stream retry as "blocked / needs input", red state + notification sound, with no way to know it recovered).

One correction to my own body text: I wrote that child events carry "only the child's sessionID and parentID" — that's true for `session.created` only; `session.status` carries neither, which matches #30043.

If maintainers prefer consolidating, the "surface subagent lifecycle on the root session" ask fits as a consumer-impact case under #45549 (point 3) / #30043 — happy to move the repro there.

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #46123: Feature request to improve session list UX in the desktop app
- #27974: CLI and GUI using separate session stores (sessions not shared between CLI and Desktop)
- #6680: Viewing archived/past sessions on desktop
- #29071: Sessions created in Desktop not visible in CLI session list

For keybind-related issues (you mentioned Ctrl+Tab, Ctrl+K shortcuts), please also check our pinned keybinds documentation: #4997

If you believe this was flagged incorrectly, please let a maintainer know.

This also affects transcript viewers that use `session.time_updated` as a change-detection signal for the container.

Without a reliable session-level timestamp that envelopes child writes, viewers have to periodically scan message and part rows across every session to determine which ones changed, and that doesn't scale on large databases where OpenCode activity leads to 200-700% CPU usage, because one active session triggers a full re-read of every session's children.

Bumping `time_updated` on execution lifecycle events as suggested here would let viewers skip unchanged sessions using just the session row, without periodic full-table verification passes.

# Comment draft for OpenCode issue #36383

Issue: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/36383

I can reproduce what appears to be the same failure on a different Windows 11 + Radeon 760M system, including the same five immediate GPU-process crashes with `exitCode -2147483645 (0x80000003)`.

## My environment

- Windows 11 Pro 64-bit, build 26200.9278
- AMD Ryzen 5 8600G with AMD Radeon 760M Graphics
- 32 GB RAM
- AMD Radeon driver `32.0.31041.1004`, dated 2026-08-17
- OpenCode Desktop `1.18.26` (updated from 1.18.25)
- dxdiag reports: `Display Tab 1: No problems found`

The repeated log entry is:

```text
(utility) child process gone {
  details: {
    type: 'GPU',
    reason: 'crashed',
    exitCode: -2147483645,
    serviceName: 'GPU'
  }
}
```

## Additional observations

- The Desktop app starts its local sidecar, but normal launches often exit before a usable window appears.
- The issue persisted after updating from 1.18.25 to 1.18.26.
- It also persisted after clearing OpenCode caches, testing a clean local profile, and temporarily closing Radeon Software, Xbox Game Bar, and Armoury Crate processes.
- `opencode serve` works correctly when launched manually, so the local CLI/server path works.
- I did not modify, roll back, or reinstall the AMD driver.
- I also have a disconnected RX 580 driver package stored on the system, but it is not active.

The only temporary command that consistently produced a visible stable Desktop window was:

```text
OpenCode.exe --no-sandbox --disable-gpu --disable-gpu-compositing
```

I do not consider `--no-sandbox` an acceptable permanent workaround because it reduces Electron/Chromium process isolation.

I have a redacted technical report, log excerpts, a debug ZIP, and dxdiag information available if maintainers want them. Is there a requested diagnostic or a supported workaround for this Electron GPU-process startup failure on Radeon 760M systems?

The TUI-works / headless-run-hangs split you are seeing is the tell, and it matches what I traced on macOS.

opencode run reads stdin to EOF before it does anything else. The TUI path never does this, which is why only run hangs. If the process inherits an stdin that is open and never closes, which is the normal case for a CI runner, a background job, or an agent harness, it waits there forever. Nothing is logged past init because nothing has happened yet, and no session is created, so there is no session id to recover from afterwards.

The one-token check: add a stdin redirect and run the identical command.

  opencode run --pure --agent build -m opencode/mimo-v2.5-free "say OK" < /dev/null

On 1.18.25 here that is the whole difference. Without the redirect: exit 124 under timeout, zero bytes on stdout, empty stderr. With it: clean run. I measured 5 of 5 hangs without and 5 of 5 successes with when I first chased this, and it still reproduces the same way on 1.18.25 today.

If that fixes it for you, then it is not intermittent and it is not network, it is just whether the calling shell happened to leave stdin open. That also explains why it looked flaky across environments rather than consistently broken.

Fresh measurement on 1.18.25 in case it is useful while you are implementing: opencode agent list is now 8,724 lines / 224,677 bytes here. For trend, that is up from 8,634 lines / about 222 KB on 1.18.19 and roughly 7,000 lines on 1.18.4, so it is still growing release over release.
